species.name: Sailet

dex.text: A tiny post mill with four sails, all of them eager. It turns to face the wind, whichever way the wind goes, and takes the credit.
dex.fact: In a post mill the whole body of the mill turns on one great central post, so the miller can face the sails into the wind.

species.real: Windmills came to England in the late twelfth century, and their sails are called sweeps in some parts of the country.

species.name: Postmill

dex.text: Stands on one post and turns on it as the weather demands, covered in flour and sacks. Knows exactly which way the wind is blowing, and tells everyone.
dex.fact: A post mill is turned by pushing on a long tail pole at the back, which is why millers had to be strong as well as patient.

species.real: Bourn Windmill in Cambridgeshire, dated to 1636, is often described as among the oldest surviving post mills in the country.
